raw_segments.text: The Constitution had not destroyed the distinct sovereignty of the states, and all communities,
of whatever nature they may be, are impelled by a secret propensity to assert their independence.
This propensity is still more decided in a country like America, in which every village
forms a sort of republic accustomed to conduct its own affairs.
It therefore costs the states an effort to submit to the federal supremacy, and all efforts,
however successful they may be, necessarily subside with the causes in which they originated.
